newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin says U.S.-Russia summit hard but important.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin says U.S.-Russia summit hard but important.

text.p: The Kremlin on Tuesday defended President Boris Yeltsin's performance at last week's Helsinki summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton and said the meeting had been their toughest and most important so far.
"In these conditions, Boris Yeltsin proved himself a skillful diplomat and negotiator, able to obtain the most possible," presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.

Despite charges by the communist opposition that Yeltsin betrayed Russia's interests by compromising over NATO's plans to expand eastwards, Yastrzhembsky said both presidents had defended their ground firmly at the meeting.
"Historians may one day call the Helsinki summit the most important in Russian-American relations in the post-confrontation period," he said.
The Helsinki summit was the 11th between Clinton and Yeltsin.
Yeltsin dropped a demand that any deal it concludes with NATO outlining ties with the Western defence alliance must be legally binding, saying instead that it has only to be politically binding.

This means the deal, which both sides hope to reach before NATO offers invitations to some eastern European countries in July, can be signed by state leaders and need not be ratified by national parliaments.
Russia says NATO's plans to offer membership to former Soviet bloc countries endangers its security.

"Compromise solutions had to be found...to avoid a senseless worsening in relations between Russia and the West, and between Russia and the United States, and to avoid a degeneration into confrontation," Yastrzhembsky said.
